collections_index-lede: Collections are themed sets of places put together by travellers themselves: a weekend route, the abandoned factories of one region, the caves of the Urals or the manors along a single road. Every collection has a map with all its points, photos and the author's description, so it is easy to plan a whole trip from it instead of looking places up one by one. Any registered user can put together a collection of their own from the places on the site.

abandoned.title: Abandoned
abandoned.content: Abandoned and destroyed buildings, complexes and structures of historical, cultural or architectural significance. These objects reflect past eras and events, being witnesses of time and change. Abandoned structures may include abandoned factories, castles, estates, churches, bunkers and other architectural sites that attract the attention of researchers, historians and lovers of abandoned places.

archeology.title: Archeology
archeology.content: This category presents various archaeological sites, including ancient settlements, dolmens, sites of primitive people and other interesting places related to the history and culture of various eras. This includes unique artifacts, remains of ancient civilizations, religious buildings such as obelisks and megalithic monuments, as well as historical excavation sites, petroglyphs, and underwater archaeological finds.

architecture.title: Architecture
architecture.content: Buildings worth a detour: Soviet modernism and constructivism, wooden architecture with carved window frames, eccentric houses and buildings of unusual shapes. This is architecture that rarely makes it into guidebooks but sticks in the memory at first sight: bold concrete forms, mosaics on facades, old merchant houses and structures built by enthusiasts to their own design.

artwork.title: Art object
artwork.content: Unusual sculptures and monuments, street art, Soviet mosaics, land art and open-air art objects. These are places where art leaves the museums for the streets and fields: strange, funny or touching monuments, huge installations and murals. Many of them were made by local craftsmen and are known only to the people living nearby, while some have long become symbols of their towns.

camping.title: Camping (Vacation place)
camping.content: Various campsites and campgrounds where visitors can spend the night in tents, RVs or motorhomes. These places provide amenities for temporary outdoor living and provide opportunities for travelers to enjoy nature, relax, and spend time outdoors. Campsites are usually equipped with fire pits, cooking areas, toilets, showers and amenities for a comfortable stay. Tent cities offer more compact tent sites and accommodate both campers and campers.

castle.title: Fortress (Castle)
castle.content: Various types of castles, palaces, fortresses, estates, stately homes, kremlins and other historical buildings. These architectural sites are important historical and cultural monuments, reflecting the wealth and grandeur of past eras. Castles and fortresses often served as defensive structures that protected the territory from enemy attacks, while palaces and estates were the residences of noble families and aristocracy.

cave.title: Cave (Grotto)
cave.content: Natural formations such as caves, small grottoes and sinkholes that are formed naturally and provide opportunities for exploration. These places are unique and mysterious, have beauty and mysticism, and provide an opportunity to plunge into the mysterious world of underground spaces. In addition, this category may also include man-made abandoned and unused mines, horizontal adits that are open and accessible for exploration.

disaster.title: Disaster site
disaster.landing: Disasters, nuclear test sites and radiation
disaster.content: Crash and disaster sites, nuclear test sites, exclusion zones and areas of radioactive contamination, meteorite impact sites. These are traces of tragic events that changed the lives of people and the face of the land. They are reminders of the cost of mistakes and of the power of nature and technology. Visiting many of these places requires special care, and sometimes a permit.

engineering.title: Engineering
engineering.content: Lighthouses, windmills and watermills, water towers, dams, old bridges, observatories and other engineering structures. Many of them were built more than a century ago and still impress with their well-thought-out design, and some have become monuments to the engineering thought of their time. Here it is worth looking at the details: the masonry, the steel trusses, the mechanisms and the traces of how people solved technical problems without modern technology.

industrial.title: Industrial site
industrial.content: Working and abandoned factories, plants, mines, adits, quarries and spoil heaps. Industrial sites show the scale of human activity: giant workshops, deep pits, mountains of waste rock and old workings where ore, coal and stone were extracted. They attract fans of industrial aesthetics, the history of technology and unusual man-made landscapes. Many of these places are dangerous, so visit them with care.

landscape.title: Natural wonder
landscape.landing: Canyons, craters, dunes and natural landmarks
landscape.content: Canyons and gorges, craters, dunes, glaciers, geological outcrops, monumental trees and other unusual natural formations that are not mountains, caves or bodies of water. Wind, water and ice shaped these places over thousands of years, carving out landscapes that look like the set of a science fiction film. People come here for rare scenery, for the geological history written in the rock layers and for photos no one else has.

manor.title: Manor
manor.content: Noble and merchant manors, palaces, estates and country houses, both preserved and abandoned. These are main houses with colonnades, outbuildings, parks with alleys and ponds, farm buildings and the traces of a life that went on here for centuries. Many manors are associated with famous families, writers and scientists, and some became sanatoriums, schools or simply ruins after the revolution, still keeping the beauty of past eras.

memorial.title: Monument
memorial.content: Memorials and memorial complexes, monuments, obelisks, busts and mass graves erected in honor of famous people, events and the victims of wars. These places serve as reminders of the heroism and suffering brought by wars and as an expression of respect for those who gave their lives for peace and freedom. Many of them have become symbols of remembrance for their towns and villages, places of gatherings and memorial ceremonies.

military.title: Military facility
military.content: This category includes various military forts, military training grounds, bunkers (long-term firing points) and bunkers (wood-earth firing points), as well as fortifications and free-standing defensive structures of historical significance. These facilities were built to provide defense and protection of territories during different historical periods. Military forts and fortifications are important historical monuments, reflecting the military architecture and strategic thinking of the era. This category does NOT include modern and secret military facilities that are only of historical significance.

mountain.title: Mountain
mountain.content: Various mountain formations and landscapes, including cliffs, cliffs, mountain peaks, hills, mountain peaks and ridges. These natural formations are important elements of the landscape, reflecting natural geological processes and the history of the formation of the earth's crust. Mountain landscapes are objects of admiration for tourists and outdoor enthusiasts, providing opportunities for mountaineering, rock climbing, hiking and enjoying picturesque views of the surrounding nature.

museum.title: Museum
museum.content: Unusual and private museums, open-air museums, exhibition halls, zoos and animal parks. Here you can see exhibits from different eras, old machinery and everyday objects, works of art, and get to know the animal world. Small museums created by enthusiasts are especially valuable: they often keep things and stories that cannot be found anywhere else.

mystic.title: Anomalous place
mystic.content: Places of power, anomalous zones and places surrounded by legends: "cursed" forests, mysterious stones, tracts with a bad reputation and spots where, as the stories go, inexplicable things happen. What matters here is the story: local legends, rumors and eyewitness accounts. Whether to believe them is up to you, but visiting such a place and forming your own opinion is interesting for any traveler.

religious.title: Religious building
religious.content: Churches, mosques, monasteries, chapels and temples of historical significance, including both active and historical religious buildings of various faiths. These buildings are witnesses to the history and culture of peoples, architectural masterpieces and places of spiritual worship. They preserve the rich heritage of past times and reflect religious traditions and customs.

spring.title: Spring (Source)
spring.content: Springs, wells and holy springs, mineral and hot springs, geysers and other places where groundwater comes to the surface. Many springs offer clean drinking water, holy springs often have a chapel and a bathing font, and hot springs and geysers are a rare natural phenomenon worth travelling far for. In some cases this also includes man-made standpipes, but only in hard-to-reach places where they become a landmark of their own.

transport.title: Vehicles
transport.content: Vehicles on pedestals, ship and aircraft graveyards, abandoned railways, locomotives and other vehicles that have become landmarks. This includes tanks and aircraft monuments, ships moored or stranded on the shore, abandoned carriages and narrow-gauge railways lost in the forest. These objects tell the story of technology and transport, and many of them have become symbols of their era and their towns.

viewpoint.title: Viewpoint
viewpoint.content: Places with the widest view: lookout points on hills and cliffs, observation towers, rooftops and spots overlooking a river, a valley or a city. These are places worth climbing up to: at sunrise, at sunset or on a clear day you can see for tens of kilometers. They are the best way to understand the lie of the land, take a panorama, or simply stand above the world for a while.

water.title: Water
water.content: Water bodies such as lakes, rivers, reservoirs, ponds and other bodies of water that are suitable for recreation, fishing, and camping. Reservoirs in this category must be part of the natural landscape and play an important role in the biological and ecological diversity of the region. This category should not include artificial hydraulic structures, such as treatment plants, settling tanks and other similar reservoirs.

waterfall.title: Waterfall
waterfall.content: This category includes various natural waterfalls - unique natural formations characterized by water falling from a height and creating characteristic sound effects. Natural waterfalls are the result of natural processes such as erosion and hydrological phenomena and are important components of ecosystems. They are of interest to tourists and the scientific community as objects of beauty and research.
